messages.subject: Small inconsistencies in GGIR Vignette
parts:
Hi

I'm starting to learn the GGIR package. On the vignette (
Accelerometer data processing with GGIR (r-project.org) ) it is written:

"If you are only interested in parameter “HASIB.algo” from the sleep_params object:
library(GGIR) 
print(load_params()$params_sleep[["HASPT.algo"]])"

So there is first HASIB.algo referenced instead of HASPT.ago (which also exists) and also it's sleep_params in the explanation but $params_sleep in the function call.

It's no big deal, but I think this might be a small inconsistency that could be fixed?

Best regards and thanks for the great package, as far as I have seen =)
Chris

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Small inconsistencies in GGIR Vignette
parts:
If you are only interested in parameter “HASIB.algo” from the sleep_params object:
library(GGIR)
print(load_params()$params_sleep[["HASPT.algo"]])"
​

For historical reasons these are correct, although I agree that it is somewhat confusing. 
Arguments mvpathreshold and boutcriter are only used in GGIR part 2, while threshold.bout and boutcriter.mvpa are only used in GGIR part 5. This is documented in the parameters vignette. 

Background: When I first implemented part 2 in 2012 I did not expect to ever be working with more than one threshold. However, when I implemented part 5 I realised that having one argument was not practical.  So, one solution for the future could be to slowly deprecate the old arguments and make threshold.mod work for both part 2 and 5, but obviously that would then have to come with clear warning to the user and good documentation to avoid any misunderstanding.

Vincent
